statement: 4 In [15], the graph is actually a pruned random graph, in which o(n) edges are removed; this does not affect compatibility with our results, as the LP value is Lipschitz and so the pruning changes the LP value by o(1). 5 The expert may notice that we require the number of clauses m ndk/2e , whereas the best Sum-of- Squares and spectral algorithms require only m nk/2 . This is because we do not know how to relate the Sherali–Adams value of the objective function to its square (local versions of the Cauchy-Schwarz argument result in a loss). Such a relation would allow us to apply our techniques immediately to prove that Sherali–Adams matches the SOS and spectral performance for odd as well as even k. 6 Though for 2-xor and max-cut we have done this explicitly, for higher-arity random CSPs we have left this for the interested reader.

CCC 2019 1.2 Prior work It is a folklore result that in random graphs with average degree nδ , 3-round Sherali–Adams certifies a max-cut value of at most max(1 − Ω(δ), 32 ) (observed for the special case of δ > 12 in [6, 39]); this is simply because of concentration phenomena, since most edges participate in roughly the same number of odd cycles of length O( 1δ ) ≥ 3, after which one can apply the triangle inequality. However this observation does not allow one to take the refutation strength independent of the average degree.
